extracted.intended_audience: scholars and students in communication/media studies (interested in framing theory and frame analysis)
extracted.subtask_description: Critical summary and assessment of Robert M. Entman's 1993 framing article, its key definitional claims (including four frame elements and two definitions), and its conceptual and methodological impact on frame analysis research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entman's four frame elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Entman's distinction of four frame elements that constitute what frames do in news/discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonly paraphrased from Entman (1993): frames "define problems, diagnose causes, make moral judgments, and suggest remedies." Use these four functions as diagnostic dimensions when identifying or coding frames in texts or news messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entman's two definitions of framing
rubrics_metrics.description: The chapter highlights that Entman offered two related definitions of framing in his influential article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One definition emphasizes selection and salience (i.e., to frame is to select some aspects of perceived reality and make them more salient). The second operationalizes framing via the four frame elements (problem definition, causal interpretation, moral evaluation, treatment recommendation). Both definitions are treated as central to applying the framing concept in empirical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual and definitional clarity as an evaluative criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Entman's article is evaluated for its conceptual–definitional contribution: clarifying a fractured paradigm and supplying usable definitional tools for framing research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing framing scholarship, judge whether the work advances definitional precision (e.g., clear statements of what constitutes a frame, how framing differs from related constructs) and whether it situates itself relative to prior and contemporaneous work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological impact and methodological questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The chapter assesses Entman's methodological impact on how researchers identify and measure frames and notes that methodological (empirical) questions arise from his conceptualization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate frame studies on the rigor of their empirical methods (e.g., coding procedures, operationalization of frame elements) and whether they address known methodological challenges. The chapter links to later methodological literature (e.g., Pan & Kosicki; David et al.; Matthes & Kohring) that seeks to improve frame-analysis methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing (press–state relation) as a framing-related concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexing is cited and given a definitional statement: "Mass media news professionals, from the boardroom to the beat, tend to 'index' the range of voices and viewpoints in both news and editorials according to the range of views expressed in mainstream government debate about a given topic" (Bennett 1990, p.106).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use indexing as an evaluative/explanatory concept when analyzing whose perspectives are included or excluded in news frames, especially in studies of press–state relations and elite-driven framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability and validity in content analysis of media frames
rubrics_metrics.description: The chapter cites literature that frames content analysis must aim to improve reliability and validity when identifying frames in media content (see Matthes & Kohring 2008).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a methodological rubric, require that frame-content analyses report coding schemes, intercoder reliability, validity checks, and clear operational definitions tied to the conceptual frame elements to ensure trustworthy results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame resonance and mobilization (evaluating frame effectiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The chapter references theoretical work on frame resonance, ideology, and mobilization (e.g., Benford & Snow; Snow & Benford), indicating effectiveness criteria for frames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating the power or effect of a frame, consider its resonance with target audiences (cultural meanings, values), capacity to mobilize participants, and empirical effects on attitudes and behavior (as in studies of framing effects and public opinion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to agenda-setting and priming (situating framing among media effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: The text links framing to related media-effects concepts such as agenda-setting and priming (e.g., Iyengar & Simon 1993; Price & Tewksbury 1997).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In evaluating framing research, assess whether authors properly distinguish framing from agenda-setting and priming, and whether their hypotheses and methods account for overlaps and differences between these constructs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to contemporary societal discourses (external validity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The chapter asks whether Entman's article 'still tells us something today' and discusses application to contemporary issues such as climate change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use applicability to current societal discourses as a criterion: test whether framing concepts and methods translate to new media environments and contemporary topics (e.g., transnational/digital media, climate discourse) and whether studies address context-specific dynamics.
